 J U D G M E N T
This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of .32,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 09122019 about 8.25 A.M., the Petitioner was waiting for the clearance of signal with his motorcycle bearing No.KA41EP2045 near Pai Mobile showroom, Opposite to Big Bazaar, Kathriguppe, Bengaluru, the driver of Honda car bearing No.KA05MY1195 (herein after called as offending vehicle) drove the same in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down under the wheels of the car and sustained grievous injuries and motorcycle was completely damaged.
Immediately he was taken to Yogananda hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
It is claimed that Petitioner has spent more than .50,000/ for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 25 years, was a private employee and earning .50,000/ p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
He is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 insurer and Respondent No.2owner.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
4. The Respondent No.1Insurance company filed its objection denying the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the negligence of the driver of offending car and contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of Petitioner himself.
It has contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of motorcycle were not arrayed as Respondents in the petition.
It has contended that the driver of offending car was not holding valid DL and concerned police have filed charge sheet U/s.3(1), 181 of MV Act.
It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for Subrahmanya.
S vs Iffco Tokio Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd

on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68017871/
2 dismissal of the petition.
5. Respondent No.2owner has filed his written statement denying the grievous injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
She has admitted that she is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.1 and policy was valid as on the date of accident.
It is contended that the accident was not due to her negligence.
On the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence of the Petitioner himself.
Further it is contended that she has paid the medical expenses of the Petitioner and also paid repair charges of his bike.
She has contended that the Petitioner has sustained only simple injuries and not taken any inpatient treatment and denied the other averments of the petition.
The compensation claimed is exaggerated and without any basis and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.Whether the Petitioner proves that on 09122019 about 8.25 a.m. when he was returning to home in his bike bearing No.KA41EP2045, near Pai Junction,
Opposite to Big Bazar, Kathriguppe, Bengaluru, the second Respondent who is the owner of the Honda Car bearing Reg.No.KA 05MY1195 droven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner due to which Petitioner fell down came under the wheels of second Respondent's car and sustained grievous injuries?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.17.
8.
The Respondent No.1 has examined its official as RW1 and got marked the copy of policy at Ex.R.1.
9. I have heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

He has deposed that on 09122019 Subrahmanya.S vs Iffco Tokio Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68017871/
3

about 8.25 A.M., he was waiting for the clearance of signal with his motorcycle bearing No.KA41 EP2045 near Pai Mobile showroom, Opposite to Big Bazaar, Kathriguppe, Bengaluru, the driver of Honda car bearing No.KA05MY1195 drove the same in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed to his motorcycle.
Due to the impact, he fell down under the wheels of the car and sustained grievous injuries and his motorcycle was completely damaged.
It is stated that the the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending car.

12. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, complaint at Ex.P2, spot mahazar at Ex.P3, sketch at Ex.P4, notice and reply at Ex.P.5 and 6, police notice to Respondent No.2 at Ex.R.7, wound certificate at Ex.P.8, IMV report at Ex.P.9 and charge sheet with statement of witnesses at Ex.P10 and Order sheet in CC.11875/2019 along with acquisition.
As per wound certificate he has sustained multiple contused abrasions present right forehead, cheek and right elbow and blunt injuries to the chest and abdomen.
13. RespondentInsurance company denied the negligence of car driver and contended that it was the negligence of Petitioner/rider of twowheeler.
During cross examination of PW1, it was suggested that he was going in high speed and suddenly applied brake in the signal due to which accident occurred.
Petitioner denied the same.

Respondent No.2owner crossexamined the PW1 and suggested that car was on the right side and Petitioner was trying to overtake the car from left side, while doing so rare wheel of the car has touched the motorcycle.
It is also suggested that if the car was in high speed, it would have dashed other vehicles also.
It is contended that the Petitioner tried to overtake the car from left side, dashed the footpath and fell near the rare wheel of the car.
14. Second Respondent has stated in her written statement that she took the injured to the hospital and paid medical expenses and also auto charges.
She alleges that he had sustained simple injuries and there was no need of admission in the hospital.
Only to extract compensation, he got admitted in the hospital.
Respondent No.2 was driving the offending car as on the date of accident and denied her negligence here in this petition.
But for Magistrate she has pleaded guilty paid fine for the offences alleged U/s.279 and 337 of IPC and Sec.3(1) R/w 181 of MV Act.
She has not stepped into the witness box and not deposed that it was not her negligence.
She has failed to disprove her negligence.
Police have found her negligent and filed charge sheet against her, which is not challenged.
However, the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident is not disputed.
Respondents have not lead any evidence to prove the negligence of rider of the motorcycle.
15. The evidence of PW1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the Respondent No.2.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As it is held in Issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, the Petitioner is entitled to get compensation.

Subrahmanya.S vs Iffco Tokio Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68017871/
4 17.

So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of .20,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in road traffic accident and submitted that he has spent .50,000/ towards treatment, nourishment, conveyance and other charges.
The Petitioner has produced duplicate medical bills and vehicle repair bill at Ex.P17 to show the expenses incurred by him.
The Ex.P.13 discharge summary shows that Petitioner has sustained multiple injuries to face, chest and elbow and he was treated as an inpatient in Yogananda hospital from 09122019 to 10 122019.
There are no evidence that the Petitioner has sustained any disability as he has not examined the doctor.
There are no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect his livelihood and daytoday activities and earning capacity.
The injuries do not appear to be much grievous causing disability to the Petitioner as the wound certificate shows the injuries are simple in nature.
18. Petitioner says that he has spent .50,000/ for medical and other expenses, but the original bills are not produced.
It appears that the Petitioner has got reimbursement of those medical bills.
He has not produced any documentary evidence to show that he has not got reimbursed medical bills.
Petitioner has stated that his spectacles were broken in the accident and he purchased new one and bill for that is produced at Ex.P.17 for .4,900/.
The police and medical records do not show that spectacles were broken in the accident.
Further he has produced vehicle repair charges which appears to have been paid by insurer of motorcycle.
He has not produced any material evidences to show that he has paid .8,000/ and Insurance company has paid .6,000/ as he stated in his evidence.
19. However, as discussed earlier absolutely there are no materials to show loss of earning capacity to the Petitioner.

By considering the nature of injuries, 1 day admission in the hospital, pain and sufferings by the Petitioner and considering other incidental expenses, I think this would be a proper case to award global compensation.

By taking into consideration all the factors, I deem it appropriate to award .30,000/ as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
20. Liability:
As it is already held in Issue No.1 that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the car by Respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 insurer of the offending vehicle has contended that they are not liable to pay any compensation as Respondent No.2 had no DL to drive the car as on the date of accident.
Since it is a violation of condition of policy, it is contended that the Respondent No.2 alone shall pay the compensation and the insurance company shall be exonerated from the liability.

RW1 / official from the insurance company has deposed that the charge sheet is filed against the Respondent No.2 alleging offence U/s.3 R/w 181 of MV Act and she has pleaded guilty before Magistrate also.
The Respondent No.2 has contested the petition and filed her written statement.
She being driver cum owner of offending car, has complete knowledge of this petition.
The Petitioner has sought for order of pay and recovery from the insurance company in case of allowing petition.
But the Respondent No.2 being a responsible citizen has drove the car without having license and violated the traffic rules as well as terms of insurance policy.

Since the Petitioner is awarded only a global compensation of .30,000/, it would be just and reasonable to direct the Respondent No.2 alone to pay the compensation in lieu of breach of contract of insurance policy.

For these reasons, I hold that the Respondent No.2 being the driver cum owner of offending Subrahmanya.S vs Iffco Tokio Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68017871/
5 car is liable to pay the above compensation with interest at 6% p.a. to the Petitioner.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
21.ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost against the Respondent No.2 only.
Petition against the Respondent No.1 is dismissed.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .30,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this Order.
On deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount along with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
 Advocate's fee is fixed at  .1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 20 th day of January 2023).
(DIVYASHREE C.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACMM Member, MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru ANNEXURE
